explanations.3: This points to a Docker Compose file one level up from the current directory, which defines the containers that will run your development environment.
explanations.8: This automatically adjusts the user ID inside the container to match your host machine, preventing file permission issues when you edit code.
explanations.12: The ${dirty} and ${rootName} are placeholders that VS Code replaces with actual values—like showing a dot when files have unsaved changes.
explanations.14: This tells VS Code to automatically open the terminal panel when you first start the dev container, so you can run commands right away.
explanations.19: This command runs automatically after the container is created, installing all your Python dependencies from the requirements file into the container.
